provision_review.why: Section 1102(d)(1) lets the Director set the table ceiling anywhere from $20,000 to $60,000. The pre-fix rule treats $60,000 as a fixed ceiling (table method if taxable income is at or below $60,000, schedule method above it). That asserts the table method across the whole $20,000-$60,000 band, which the text leaves undecided. The post-fix rule adds the $20,000 floor and an 'uncertain' status for that band.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module encoded 30 Del. C. §1102(d)(1) as "table method applies iff taxable income <= $60,000", dropping the statute's qualifying clause that the Director may instead set a lesser tax-table-income ceiling "but in any event not less than $20,000", so it asserted the table method (and, by complement, capped credits against schedule tax) across the whole $20,000-$60,000 band where the source does not establish which method controls.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release: §1102(d)(1) verbatim is "...whose tax table income for the taxable year does not exceed $60,000, or such lesser amount as the Director may determine but in any event not less than $20,000, a tax determined under tables... prescribed by the Director of Revenue." Pre-fix rules were `de_pit_2026_tax_table_method_applies: taxable_income <= de_pit_2026_tax_table_income_ceiling (60000)` and `de_pit_2026_schedule_method_controls: taxable_income > 60000`; post-fix adds parameter `de_pit_2026_minimum_director_tax_table_income_ceiling = 20000` (proof atom excerpt "but in any event not less than $20,000") and splits into three mutually exclusive statuses, and the three credit rules now return 0 unless `de_pit_2026_definite_schedule_method_controls`, so credits are no longer capped against a schedule amount in the uncertain band. Kind is a judgment call between unrepresented_clause (the Director-lesser-ceiling clause was absent and the fix adds it, which is how I labeled it) and untraceable_branch (the pre-fix table/schedule status branch asserted more than the cited source supports); the numeric $60,000 itself was never wrong. This commit is a multi-thread hardening of a single module and also carries: (a) a second fidelity-relevant scope/logic thread — the supported-profile guard moved from fail-open `<= 0` comparisons to exact `== 0` plus a new nonnegative input-domain guard and newly required conditions (`is_full_year_resident`, `not is_joint_return`, `elects_standard_deduction`, `not uses_separate_spouse_mechanics`, `not has_section_1102_b_lump_sum_distribution`), i.e. the module previously produced full-year non-joint standard-deduction numbers without checking that profile and treated negative category amounts as in-profile (this alone would read as polarity_or_logic / wrong_entity_or_scope); (b) boundary-disclosure relabeling of three inputs the module had presented as raw but that are caller-completed (`fiduciary_adjustment` -> `completed_section_1634_fiduciary_adjustment`, `taxable_income_from_other_jurisdiction` -> `completed_section_1122_other_jurisdiction_taxable_income`, `potential_low_income_age_or_disability_exclusion` -> `completed_low_income_age_or_disability_exclusion_trigger`); (c) a purely mechanical/provenance layer — pervasive `profile_candidate_*` renames, expanded summary/rationale prose, and many added exact-subsection proof-atom excerpts. Defect was caught by pre-merge review inside PR #1027, so the defective state (669d5eb4) never reached main; if the corpus requires defects that were merged, flag this. Companion test file gained 737 lines and the apply manifest was regenerated; no other module changed.
triage.verifier_justification: The pinned corpus text of 30 Del. C. §1102(d)(1) reads "whose tax table income for the taxable year does not exceed $60,000, or such lesser amount as the Director may determine but in any event not less than $20,000" — so the source fixes only a band ($20,000–$60,000) within which the operative table ceiling lies, and does not establish which method controls above $20,000. The pre-fix module dropped that qualifying clause entirely (its proof atom excerpt was only "tax table income for the taxable year does not exceed $60,000") and encoded a definite public judgment `de_pit_2026_tax_table_method_applies = taxable_income <= 60000`, with the complement `schedule_method_controls = taxable_income > 60000`; its summary even asserted "For taxable income at or below $60,000, section 1102(d) requires a Director-prescribed table", which the statute does not say. The fix adds the missing clause as a grounded parameter (`de_pit_2026_minimum_director_tax_table_income_ceiling = 20000`, proof excerpt "but in any event not less than $20,000") and splits the single boolean into three mutually exclusive statuses, adding the previously absent uncertain $20k–$60k branch. I tried to refute this as mere added precision, but the pre-fix rule made an affirmative, exposed status claim across the whole band, so this corrects encoded meaning rather than adding coverage the module never claimed.

-        formula: de_pit_2026_taxable_income <= de_pit_2026_tax_table_income_ceiling
+            source: {corpus_citation_path: us-de/statute/30/1102, excerpt: "but in any event not less than $20,000"}
triage.verifier_notes: Kinds I ruled out: amount_mismatch (the $60,000 is verbatim in the source and was not wrong; $20,000 is new, from the omitted clause); boundary_direction (strictness stayed `<=`/`>` on both sides — the change is a new threshold created by the added clause, not a flipped bound); untraceable_branch (the `<= $60,000` branch did have source basis, it was just unqualified). Caveat for the reviewer: a defensible counter-reading is that $60,000 is the statutory default and the Director's lesser determination is an unexercised external fact, which would make the pre-fix a defensible default rather than a wrong encoding — I weighted against it because the module's own source_verification declares the 2026 Director ceiling absent from the pinned corpus, so asserting the maximum-ceiling reading as definite exceeds the source. Also note this commit bundles at least two further distinct fidelity issues named in the same PR-body sentence that are NOT covered by the flagged rule_path: (1) the fail-open profile guard, `de_pit_2026_federal_nol_carryback_deduction <= 0` → `== 0` plus a new `de_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` nonnegativity conjunct (polarity_or_logic); (2) credits previously capped unconditionally against schedule tax, now gated on `if de_pit_2026_definite_schedule_method_controls:` (also polarity/scope). If the corpus wants one kind per commit, unrepresented_clause is correct for the flagged rule; if it admits multiple, the fail-closed change deserves its own entry.
